chapters.n: John, calling himself “the elder,” writes to “the elect lady and her children.” This may be a real woman and her family or, as many think, a local congregation and its members.

f.g: Greek presbyteros — an older, senior leader; traditionally the Apostle John.
Chosen lady; possibly a symbolic name for a congregation.

chapters.n: His love for them is grounded in the truth of the gospel that lives in believers and will remain forever.
John blesses them with grace, mercy, and peace from the Father and the Son, flowing in truth and love.

f.w: Grace be with you, mercy, and peace

chapters.n: He was overjoyed to find some of her children living by the truth, just as the Father commanded.
He asks them to keep the commandment they had from the start: love one another.
Love means living by God’s commandments, and His commandment is to walk in love.
Many deceivers deny that Jesus Christ came in a real human body. Such a person is a deceiver and an antichrist.
Watch yourselves so you don’t lose what you have worked for, but receive your full reward.
Anyone who “goes too far” and leaves Christ’s teaching does not have God. Whoever stays in His doctrine has both the Father and the Son.

f.g: Goes beyond, ‘runs ahead’—leaving true doctrine for something supposedly more advanced.

chapters.n: Don’t welcome traveling false teachers into your home or give them your blessing. House churches met in homes, so hosting a teacher meant endorsing him.

f.g: A greeting wishing success—here, a sign of support.

chapters.n: Supporting such a teacher makes you a partner in the harm he does.
John has much more to say, but would rather not use paper and ink. He hopes to visit and talk face to face so their joy can be complete.

f.g: Papyrus sheets and ink of soot and gum.

chapters.n: The children of her chosen sister send greetings—perhaps members of John’s own congregation greeting a sister church.
